# Joint low-cost capability evaluation

This suite asks fixed visible-source reasoning questions in small batches and scores every
question independently. Candidate responses must be a JSON ID-to-answer mapping. Multiple-choice
items use exact option scoring; mathematical items use conservative normalized exact-answer
scoring. Completed malformed or omitted answers score zero, while gateway failures remain
incomplete. `run.py` writes results atomically after every batch.

The pilot uses four questions per candidate call with an 8,192-token ceiling. The final frozen
version will document its coding and professional-work probes and fixed domain weights here.

# Joint low-cost capability evaluation

This joint suite contains 132 independently scored questions:

- reasoning: 24 transformed multiple-choice questions from the exact June 2026 ArXivMath set and
  56 deterministic, category-stratified multiple-choice questions from HLE text-only;
- coding: 20 target-derived debugging, repository, shell, API, and implementation-invariant
  questions based on the supplied Terminal-Bench and DeepSWE task families;
- co-work: 16 objective professional calculations/judgments and 16 rubric dimensions across two
  compact professional deliverables.

Objective questions are isolated into one candidate call each and exact-scored. This prevents a
single long reasoning trace from erasing unrelated answers. Calls run at the contract's maximum
concurrency of two. ArXiv items allow 4,096 output tokens, HLE items 2,048, and coding/co-work
objective items 1,024. Each professional scenario allows 4,096 tokens and is independently scored
on eight frozen criteria by `helper-grader`; candidate and grader evidence are both retained.

The maximum declared candidate output allowance is 258,048 tokens, plus two 4,096-token grader
allowances. At the highest supplied helper price and observed candidate price class this remains
comfortably below the USD 30 whole-program cap. Actual usage can be much lower when a model reaches
answers early.

The reasoning domain gives equal total weight to ArXivMath and HLE. The co-work domain gives equal
total weight to objective probes and professional rubric dimensions. Coding items are equally
weighted. Completed malformed, omitted, or refused answers score zero; gateway or helper API
failures remain explicitly incomplete. `run.py` persists results atomically after every completed
call. No network or mutable external asset is used.

# Joint low-cost capability evaluation

This frozen joint suite contains 150 independently scored questions:

- reasoning: 24 transformed multiple-choice questions from the exact June 2026 ArXivMath set and
  58 HLE multiple-choice questions (56 deterministic category-stratified questions plus two
  sustained-reasoning questions);
- coding: 20 debugging, repository, shell, API, and implementation-invariant questions derived
  from the supplied Terminal-Bench and DeepSWE task families;
- co-work: 16 objective professional calculations/judgments and 32 rubric dimensions across four
  constrained professional deliverables.

Every objective question is isolated and exact-scored. Most ArXiv questions allow 4,096 output
tokens and most HLE questions 2,048. Four ArXiv questions receive 45,000--131,072 tokens because the
supplied historical target traces show correct answers emerging only after sustained reasoning;
two HLE questions receive 50,000. Coding and objective work questions allow 1,024. Each professional
scenario allows 30,000 tokens and is independently scored on eight frozen criteria by the
`helper-grader`, with an 8,192-token grader ceiling. Candidate and grader evidence are both retained.

The maximum candidate output allowance is 829,544 tokens and the maximum helper output allowance is
32,768. At the most expensive supplied development price ($5/M input and $30/M output), even all
output ceilings plus the fixed prompts and worst-case grader input remain below the $30 whole-suite
cap. Typical usage is much lower when a model answers early. Calls run at the allowed concurrency of
two, and results are atomically persisted after each completed call.

The frozen reasoning score weights ArXiv 40%, HLE 40%, and reused coding questions 20%. The coding
score weights core coding probes 60% and reuses ArXiv/HLE reasoning observations for 40% to reduce
the conceptual-probe ceiling without duplicate calls. The co-work score weights objective checks
10% and the four professional scenarios 90%. A declared item reused across domains is still called
only once.

Completed malformed, omitted, refused, or empty answers score zero. Gateway or helper failures remain
explicitly incomplete. No network access, mutable external asset, candidate identity, or undisclosed
label is used. `predictor.py` separately calibrates each visible target from a small set of frozen,
positive, ridge-shrunk source composites.
